photos.c: Philip Goedluck sprinted his way to some fabulous performances in open competition this summer. He was 3rd in the English Schools Intermediate Boys 100m in 11.0 and won the Southern Youths 100m in 11.25 with a 2nd place in the 200 a week later. Then after coming second in a Youth's Inter County match in 11.2 he hit the best form of his young life to win the AAA's Youths 100m title in 10.77(+3.3w) following a legal p.b. and new Club Age Record of 10.96 in the heats. Philip was also 3rd in the AAA's Youth's 200m in 22.19 - again following a p.b. and Club Youth's Record of 22.14 in the heats.

A highlight of this years BAL matches has been the sprints and relays with Todd Bennett turning out for Southampton and Ernest for Belgrave. In the final Match our sprint relay squad just held off a classy Southampton squad, broke the Div 3 record & sliced a huge 1.2 secs off the Club record. Todd hands to Roger Black and Ernie to Phil Goedluck.
MUSCLE BOYS :: "JUNIOR" ATHLETES MARCUS ADAM And PHIL GOEDLUCK SHOW THAT THEY HAVE ARM AS WELL AS LEG POWER - WATCH OUT KEN ONUAGULUCHI..
Above: Always near the top of our sprint rankings, Phil Goedluck takes the curve in a Budapest non-scoring 200m.
Left: the fastest Belgrave sprint relay squad of all time - left to right - Neil Owen, John Regis, Lenny Paul, Phil Goedluck - 40.05!

Last leg of the 4 x 100 metres under threatening skies at the Guardian Gold Cup Final at Bedford. Belgrave Harriers on the inside lane, with Phil Goedluck in command, head the charge for the line and they won the race in 41.17 but overall winners were Thames Valley Harriers.

Below: The season comes to a close with Pat's Brats celebrating their second successive Rosenheim Final victory. Left to right - Jamie Webb, ? (obscured), Marlon Dickson, Matt George, Phil Goedluck, Mike Small, Pat Mead, Marcello Bizio (obscured), Roger Alsop, Jim Braben, Pete Mercer, Dave Pamah, Dalton Powell, Richard David.

Back Page: What a Club man. Phil Goedluck seems to have given a lifetime of competing in our British League events and at the 1995 A.G.M. his contribution to our teams was officially recognised as he was elected a Vice-President of Belgrave Harriers.
Above: Phil Goedluck and Haroun Korjie hold the British Athletics League Trophy with Bruce Barton, Darryl Maynard and Neil Owen for company.
Left: Club Track & Field Captain Phil Goedluck rises toward the top of the all time points scoring list.
Darrell Maynard, Chris Rawlinson, Phil Goedluck and Noel Levy find enough energy to smile for the camera at Solihull after their 2nd place 4x400 metres relay.
